subject: chemistry

hotspots.label: The electron cloud
hotspots.description: The large, faint region around the nucleus is the electron cloud — where the electrons orbit, far outside the tiny core.
hotspots.positionHint: The large translucent sphere around the small nucleus.
hotspots.function: Shows the region where electrons orbit the nucleus.

hotspots.label: A shell layer
hotspots.description: Electrons don't orbit at random — they live in specific shell layers at fixed distances from the nucleus.
hotspots.positionHint: The distinct ring layers the electrons follow, visible when the shells layer is on.
hotspots.function: Shows electrons organized into shell layers.

hotspots.label: The electron that bonds
hotspots.description: The outermost electrons are the valence electrons — the ones that reach out and do the chemistry in every reaction.
hotspots.positionHint: The outer-shell electron reaching toward a partner, visible when the bonding layer is on.
hotspots.function: Shows the outer electrons that drive chemical reactions.

visualStyleNotes: Chemistry palette, Anatomy Atelier bar: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with a soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no props. A small nucleus with a large electron cloud floats centered, lit with soft neutral studio light — no rim-light glow, no bloom, no emissive anywhere. Clean stylized product-render look, specimen-quality not cartoon. Nucleus: soft red/gray bundle; electron cloud: large translucent warm-white shell with small teal electron dots moving through it; shell rings: thin translucent hairline circles. Strong saturated color is reserved for the small flat hotspot dots and the bonding electron (slate / amber / molecular-green accents from the Chemistry palette). Slow auto-rotation, calm, minimal chrome.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0 everywhere, single 2K shared texture atlas. Nucleus: soft red + gray spheres, roughness ~0.4. Electron dots: small muted teal spheres, roughness ~0.4. Cloud shell: translucent warm-white, alpha ~0.12. Shell rings: translucent hairline circles, alpha ~0.25. No emissive channels anywhere — any glow is handled by app runtime UI.
assetBrief:
SUBJECT: an atom focused on its electrons, built to be read as 'tiny negative particles orbiting in shells — the ones that do chemistry.' Three procedural layers, all clean primitives:

1) MAIN: a small nucleus cluster at center (a few soft red and gray spheres, radius ~0.3), surrounded by a large translucent warm-white cloud sphere (radius ~1.7, alpha ~0.12). Small muted teal electron dots (radius ~0.07) are placed on the cloud at two shell distances, drifting slowly along their ring paths (app-driven orbit).

2) SHELLS (toggleable layer): two thin translucent hairline rings appear at the shell radii, and the electron dots snap into clear positions on the rings — revealing the organized shell structure.

3) BONDING (toggleable layer): an outer-shell electron detaches and reaches toward a small partner atom appearing to one side (app animates), sharing a glow band — showing the outer electron driving a reaction.

Camera: framed so the full cloud and nucleus are visible with negative space; auto-rotate default. Budget 6-10k triangles. Named nodes: NucleusCluster, ElectronCloud, Electrons_Shell1, Electrons_Shell2, ShellRing_01, ShellRing_02, BondingElectron, PartnerAtom. All labels are hotspot dots in the app layer.
